A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same anthropomorphic-behaviour evaluation and human validation study. Their complete text, tables, figures, and appendices support comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: V1 reports original evaluations of four LLMs, human annotation studies, and an interactive validation experiment with 1,101 participants.

after.justification: V2 retains these original model-evaluation, annotation, and human-experiment results in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: The simulated-user dialogue procedure, 14 behaviours, three Judge LLMs, pronoun counting, and majority aggregation remain unchanged. AnthroBench naming, reusable-classifier descriptions, and newly printed judge instructions do not establish an algorithm change.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same four use domains, eight scenarios, and 14 behaviours, with the same English-language human validation. Therapy, companionship, and other applications newly discussed in v2 are proposed uses, not added evaluations.

E2.justification: The four target models remain unchanged. Judge-validation comparisons retain GPT-4 Turbo, Gemini 1.5 Flash, Claude 3.5 Sonnet, aggregated labels, and human baselines; the high-frequency, low-frequency, and unprompted Gemini comparisons are also retained.

E3.justification: Both report 960 five-turn dialogues per target model, the same model versions, annotation samples, human-study groups, 10–20-minute interactions, and outcome metrics. V2's additional scenario-assignment, interface, and instruction details document existing experiments rather than establish revised protocols.

E4.justification: Domain comparisons, first-appearance and transition analyses, judge-agreement analyses, and the prompting manipulation check are retained. The manipulation-check profiles move from v1 Appendix D.3/Figure 11 to v2 Section 6/Figure 7; this is not a new analysis.

E5.justification: Three samples per judge, significance tests, effect sizes, and agreement statistics are retained. V2 removes v1 Section 6.1's footnote reporting substantial AnthroScore dispersion and explaining the median's robustness to skewness, reducing statistical documentation without establishing a change in estimation or runs.

E6.justification: The numerical tables and plotted results are unchanged, including survey means of 4.00 versus 3.25 and the agreement and precision entries. A limited qualitative finding is removed: v1's observation that AnthroScore's standard deviation substantially exceeded its mean or median. Corrected agreement-figure placement does not introduce new results.

T1.justification: The behavioural definitions and relative-transition-probability calculation are unchanged. Neither version adds or revises formal assumptions, theorems, proofs, or derivations.

C1.justification: V2 adds an explicit contribution claim for AnthroBench as a publicly available benchmark with reusable classifiers and analysis capabilities. The principal claims about multi-turn evaluation, similar model profiles, and validation against human perceptions remain unchanged.

C2.justification: V2 explicitly identifies the single simulator and five-turn horizon as limitations and more directly links similar model profiles to common post-training approaches. It expands proposed applications and replaces v1's impact discussion of contextual desirability and vulnerable users with a misuse-focused ethics discussion.

D1.justification: V2 adds a code/evaluation-set access link, Judge LLM prompt template, human-rater guidance, experiment interface, participant instructions, survey wording, compensation, and participant-protection details. Appendices A.3–A.4 substantially improve documentation of existing procedures. V1's July–August 2024 evaluation-date disclosure is removed.

R1.justification: V2 explicitly distinguishes its construct-validated anthropomorphism evaluation from broader simulation assessments and LLM psychometrics/personality research. It removes the citations and references to Chang et al. (2023) and Weidinger et al. (2022), while retaining the principal research foundations.

P1.justification: V2 substantially revises the abstract, introductory framing, and discussion around AnthroBench and its practical uses. It reorganizes the appendices into nested sections with dedicated documentation subsections, removes acknowledgements, and replaces the Impact Statement with an Ethics Statement, while retaining much of the method/results prose.

P2.justification: V2 changes the main text from two columns to one, relocates the example dialogue and manipulation-check plots, replaces the domain-mapping table with prose, and moves/reformats prompt examples into the appendix. It adds an interface screenshot and corrects the swapped plot-caption associations in v1 Figures 9–10, now correctly matched in v2 Figures 10–11.

improvement.justification: V2 improves reproducibility through previously missing judge and human-study documentation, makes applicability limits explicit, and corrects misleading agreement-figure associations. These concrete gains outweigh the loss of the AnthroScore variability explanation. The improvement is primarily in transparency and presentation; the empirical evidence and central validation limitations remain essentially unchanged.
